message.content:
Implement a feature on the Nxeon platform (Next.js App Router + TS + Prisma + Tailwind). Work ONLY inside your worktree **/opt/nxeon-wt-idea-landings/** (full repo copy, node_modules + .env symlinked). ALL edits use absolute paths under that dir; NEVER edit /opt/nxeon. `cd /opt/nxeon-wt-idea-landings` for shell. Verify `npx tsc --noEmit`, fix type errors. Do NOT build/deploy/restart.

CARD — "Location-based landing pages": programmatic SEO pages in the pattern `(location) (service)` — e.g. "Singapore VPS Hosting", "London Game Server Hosting", "Toronto Web Hosting". Make a bunch, SEO-optimized.

REQUIREMENTS: a programmatic route (e.g. `app/(marketing)/[location]-[service]-hosting/page.tsx` or a `[slug]` route driven by a data table of location×service combos) that renders a premium, on-brand marketing landing page per combination with: unique H1/title/meta/OG per page, location + service specific copy, benefits, pricing/plan callouts pulled from real plans, FAQ, internal links, and JSON-LD structured data. Add all pages to the sitemap. Generate a solid set of combos: ~8-12 locations (Singapore, London, Frankfurt, New York, Toronto, Sydney, Tokyo, Amsterdam, Los Angeles, Mumbai...) × the core services (VPS hosting, game server hosting, web hosting, dedicated). Keep copy genuinely useful, not thin-doorway spam.

FIRST explore: how the existing marketing pages + SEO are structured (grep the marketing route group, sitemap.ts, existing landing pages like the game landing pages, how plans/prices are read). Reuse the marketing design system + components. Store the location/service matrix in a typed data file.

SCOPE (siblings run in parallel): ONLY new location-based marketing landing pages + sitemap + their data. Do NOT touch the per-server panel, carousel, deploy wizard, or pricing logic.

RETURN (final text = DATA): (1) files added/changed, 1 line each; (2) how many pages generated + the URL pattern; (3) how to test (example URLs); (4) follow-ups. No preamble.

===PLAN MODEL===
model Plan {
  id           String        @id @default(cuid())
  slug         String        @unique
  name         String
  cpuCores     Int
  ramMB        Int
  diskGB       Int
  bandwidthTB  Float         @default(1)
  priceCents   Int
  storageTier  String        @default("nvme") // "nvme" | "hdd"
  active       Boolean       @default(true)
  sortOrder    Int           @default(0)
  createdAt    DateTime      @default(now())
  servers      Server[]
  gamePlans    GamePlan[]
  // NxCloud tiers that clone/size their VM from this Plan. A backing Plan for an
  // NxCloud tier is kept `active = false` so it never shows in the VPS wizard.
  nxcloudPlans NxCloudPlan[]
}

enum ImageCategory {
  PLAIN_OS
  CONTROL_PANEL
  APPLICATION
}

/// An installable image shown in the deploy wizard. Plain OS clones `baseVmid`
/// directly; control panels / apps clone `baseVmid` then run `setupScript`
/// (cloud-init runcmd) to install the panel/app on first boot.
model OsTemplate {
  id              String        @id @default(cuid())
  slug            String        @unique
  name            String // display name, e.g. "Ubuntu"
  category        ImageCategory @default(PLAIN_OS)
  family          String        @default("linux") // ubuntu | debian | almalinux | rocky | cpanel | ...
  version         String        @default("") // "24.04", "13", ""
  logo            String        @default("") // icon slug for the UI
  vmid            Int // legacy/base template VMID to clone
  baseVmid        Int? // explicit base OS template for panels/apps (falls back to vmid)
  setupScript     String? // shell installed via cloud-init runcmd (panels/apps)
  minRamMB        Int           @default(1024)

I'm planning to create a typed data module defining locations and services with their metadata, plus a function to build combination slugs and generate content for each location-service pairing. Then I'll set up the dynamic route page to render these combos, though I'm pausing to reconsider the routing structure.

A top-level `[slug]` dynamic segment would coexist fine with existing static routes since static pages always take priority, and using `notFound()` for unmatched slugs actually improves 404 handling.
